correctness.rationale: Unique gap insertion histories give the exact protected-block survival product, and consequently the pair covariance factors. Harmonic expansion gives the bulk coefficient. Diagonal and off-diagonal Riemann sums converge using a uniform inverse-younger-index bound to suppress the near-origin region. Exact rational exhaustive checks (6,375 assertions) independently verify each nonasymptotic identity over enumerated small instances; finite checks are not claimed as infinite proof.

Historic implicit coverage remains a risk.

originality.rationale: The target is the fully indexed continuum covariance kernel of all birth-label prefix counts, not an unlabeled plateau count or qualitative negative association. The strongest directly compared source, Haglund–Visontai 2012, gives a stable full finite generating polynomial for value-indexed plateaux but does not evaluate the age-prefix second-order scaling kernel. Actual database and literature searches found no equivalent quantified kernel. The existing finite encoding makes the residual risk meaningful and independent review is still needed.
residual_risks: The 2012 stable multivariate generating polynomial already encodes labelled joint moments implicitly; a previous author may have specialized it to the age-prefix covariance kernel.
A complete historical search of all increasing-tree and stable-polynomial derivative papers has not been performed.
The specified-node degree PDF was searched at relevant passages rather than certified as fully excluding equivalent results.

value.rationale: The age-resolved covariance kernel quantifies the dependence of birth-era leaf/plateau survivors across arbitrary early-label subpopulations, not merely a whole-sample aggregate or a qualitative sign. The closed variance curve gives a nontrivial one-parameter profile, with a universal r-dependent exponent, and supplies benchmarks for evolving random increasing-tree statistics and prospective functional limit theory.
